headline: Revenue and profit rise on broad segment growth
summary_short: ICE's Q2 revenue of $3,611M (net revenues $2,666M after transaction-based expenses) rose 10.7% y/y (-1.5% q/q); GAAP diluted EPS of $1.69 was up 14.2% y/y (-31.9% q/q), while adjusted diluted EPS of $1.90 rose a smaller +5% y/y.
summary_long: Consolidated net revenues were $2.7 billion, +5% y/y, with growth across all three segments: Exchanges $1,464M (+3% y/y), Fixed Income and Data Services $645M (+8% y/y), and Mortgage Technology $557M (+5% y/y). GAAP operating income was $1.4 billion (+7% y/y, 52% margin); adjusted operating income was $1.6 billion (+4% y/y, 61% margin). GAAP diluted EPS of $1.69 (+14% y/y) outgrew adjusted diluted EPS of $1.90 (+5% y/y) because other income rose to $74M from $5M, mostly fair-value gains on equity investments. Cash was $1,067M against $19.8 billion of debt. ICE returned $1.8 billion to stockholders through H1, including $1.2 billion of buybacks, and raised its repurchase authorization to $4.0 billion.

drivers.explanation: CFO stated growth was recorded "across all three of our operating segments" alongside strong free cash flow generation.
Exchanges segment growth (+3% y/y) was mixed: Energy revenue fell 13% y/y while Ags and Metals (+35%), Financials (+21%) and Cash Equities (+15%) grew, per the segment revenue table.

GAAP EPS growth (+14% y/y) outpaced adjusted EPS growth (+5% y/y) because other income/(expense) swung to +$74M from +$5M, driven mainly by fair-value adjustments of equity investments per the adjusted-EPS reconciliation table.
Net income's 12.6% y/y growth is disclosed via the income statement, but the release doesn't explain the sequential decline from Q1's $1,413M since it presents only y/y comparisons.
